      "value": "This branching model is based on **GitFlow**. (See the attached diagram on this page.)

The six branch types
--------------------

| Branch | Created from | Merges into | Claude Code? | CI that runs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` (via PR) | ✅ Yes | `qa.yml` (unit tests) on PR |
| `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` (via PR) | ✅ Yes | `qa.yml` (unit tests) on PR |
| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main`**and**`develop` | ✅ Yes | `qa.yml` (unit tests) on PR |
| `release/**` | `develop` | `main` and `develop` | ⚠️ Read-only skills only | `digital-sit.yml` (full gate) + `qa.yml` (cross-browser) |
| `fix/release-{v}-*` | `release/**` | `release/**` (→ `develop` via release back-merge) | ✅ Yes | `digital-sit.yml` (full gate) on PR |
| `develop` | — | `release/**` + SIT | ❌ No | `digital-sit.yml` (full gate) on every push |

Claude Code is physically blocked from writing to `develop` or `main` via a branch-lock hook in the repo's `.claude/settings.json`.

Feature branches — day-to-day branch
------------------------------------

**When:** every task, bug fix, or experiment.

bashwide4000git checkout develop
git pull origin develop
git checkout -b feature/SFCC-123\_short-description

**Naming format:**`feature/{JIRA-KEY}_{short-description}`. Good: `feature/SFCC-456_add-back-in-stock-button`. Bad: `feature/my-changes`, `feature/fix`.

**When done:** open a PR targeting `develop`. `qa.yml` unit tests run automatically. One approval required before merge — `develop` is a shared integration point and your PR must not break it for anyone else.

**Before every session:**`git branch --show-current` (confirm branch) and `git pull origin develop` (merges happen frequently, even if you pulled this morning).

Hotfix branches — production emergencies only
---------------------------------------------

**When:** a defect in production needs an immediate fix outside the sprint cycle.

**Create from** `main` **— not** `develop`**:**

bashwide4000git checkout main
git pull origin main
git checkout -b hotfix/SFCC-999\_critical-fix-description

**Why from** `main` **not** `develop`**:**`develop` has unreleased sprint work in progress. A hotfix branched from `develop` would accidentally include unreleased features. Branching from `main` keeps the fix clean and scoped to production state only.

**Tier 1 rules still apply** — even under deadline pressure, do not modify Tier 1 files without owner approval.

**When done:** PR into `main`. After merge, the fix **must** also be back-merged to `develop` to prevent the regression re-appearing next sprint. (Merge commit vs. cherry-pick mechanism — confirm with the Integration Lead.)

Release branches — deployment targets, not working branches
-----------------------------------------------------------

**When:** a sprint is complete and a release is being promoted.

Release branches are created by squad leads or CI from a tagged `develop` state — developers do not create these. They exist as deployment targets for the SIT gate and cross-browser tests.

**Pattern:**`release/v0.1.0`, `release/digital/v1.0.0`.

**What happens here:** the full Digital SIT gate runs on every PR targeting `release/**`; BrowserStack cross-browser tests run on every PR targeting `release/**`; no new feature work goes here — only emergency release fixes after squad lead approval.

### Making a code fix on a release branch

Do not edit the release branch directly for code changes. Branch off it instead so the CI gate runs against the fix before it lands.

bashwide4000# Step 1 — branch from the release branch, not develop
git checkout release/v0.1.0
git pull origin release/v0.1.0
git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0\_short-description
# Step 2 — make the fix
# Step 3 — PR back into the release branch (not develop)
gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(checkout): SFCC-999 payment error on SIT"

Once merged, squad leads apply the same fix to `develop` via a second PR to prevent the regression re-appearing next sprint.

**When direct commits to a release branch are acceptable:** only for changes with no logic — copy corrections, version number bumps, a boolean flag toggle. These require explicit squad lead approval before committing.

**Claude Code on** `release/**`**:** supervised mode — plan first, blast-radius check, confirm before every edit. Code logic changes must go through a `fix/release-*` sub-branch as described above.

develop — the integration branch
--------------------------------

**No direct commits.** All changes arrive via PR from a `feature/*` branch. `develop` receives a deployment to Digital Dev and SIT on every push — a bad push breaks the integration environment for both squads simultaneously, which is why the PR review gate exists.

main — production state
-----------------------

**No direct commits.** All changes arrive via a release promotion or a `hotfix/*` PR. `main` always reflects the current production code. Tagging main with a semver tag (`v0.1.0`) is done by the release tooling at `scripts/tagRelease.sh`.

Tagging and versioning
----------------------

| Stage | Version format | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-go-live sprints | `v0.{sprint}.0` | `v0.1.0`, `v0.2.0` |
| Go-live | `v1.0.0` | `v1.0.0` |
| Post-go-live patches | `v1.0.{patch}` | `v1.0.1`, `v1.0.2` |

34 integrations × 7 storefronts × 5 core user journeys = **1,190 test scenarios**.

### 5.2 Entry routing

* **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
* **AU is gated** to Oceania IPs only (REG-009) but remains the x-default hreflang target, so gating runs in the application layer rather than at the network. Human visitors from outside Oceania are redirected to their matched storefront; the redirect happens on the server, so they never see AUD prices. Known search-engine and social-media preview crawlers are exempt. When a visitor cannot be confidently classified as human or bot, the system does not redirect (because incorrectly redirecting a real crawler would cost SEO).
* **Cross-region entry handling for all other storefronts** — first-visit mismatch-detection slide-out, the country/language selector, and the EU language-mismatch modal — is functional design (REG-014–035), out of scope for this TSD.

### 5.3 Single source of truth for country / locale

Country, locale, currency, shipping country, Global-e flag, and boutique-region data live in a single front-end configuration module. When a market is added, that module and the SFCC site configuration are updated together.

### 5.4 Per-storefront concerns that must not bleed

* **Consent defaults (REG-054):** per-storefront Didomi defaults are site-scoped config that must not bleed across storefronts; the values themselves are specified under REG-054.
* **Marketing opt-in default (REG-057):** site-scoped per storefront; must not bleed — value specified under REG-057.
* **Payment methods:** per-storefront Adyen configuration. Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna are post-launch.

### 5.5 Session and basket scope across storefronts

All seven storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and run on a single SFCC realm with shared customer data. This determines how a shopper's session behaves when they cross storefronts (via the country / language selector or the mismatch slide-out):

* **Session cookie is shared.** The session cookie set by the server is scoped to the single domain, so it is sent automatically on requests to any storefront prefix — no cross-domain sign-in bridge is needed.
* **Authentication tokens are site-scoped.** Each token is issued for a specific site, so the server issues a new token when a shopper switches storefronts. Because the customer record is shared across all sites, a signed-in shopper is recognised on the new storefront without re-entering credentials. A guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over.
* **Basket does not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency against its own pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency / pricebook boundary would produce incorrect pricing.
* **Checkout handoff is separate.** When an international storefront hands off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into the Global-e hosted checkout — Global-e owns that session in full.

7. Integration Map
------------------

### 7.1 Classification model

Every integration is placed in one of five **boundary classes** based on where its network call originates. The split is determined by the vendor's authentication model — a publishable key can safely be included in the browser bundle; a secret key must be kept server-side.

* **Browser-direct** — call originates from the user's browser. Vendor publishes a publishable/public key designed to ship in the JS bundle (with referrer or origin restrictions where applicable). No secret material is ever exposed.
* **MRT-mediated** — call originates from the Node layer that hosts PWA Kit (the SSR pass, a server-only proxy endpoint in the SSR/Node layer, the `/mobify/proxy/` forwarding layer, or a webhook receiver). Used whenever the vendor requires a secret token, whenever an API key must be kept off the browser bundle entirely, or whenever `httpOnly` cookies must be set or read. Credentials are held as MRT environment variables. This includes calls the PWA makes directly to MuleSoft via MRT proxy (rather than routing through SFCC).
* **SFCC-cartridge** — call originates from inside Salesforce Commerce Cloud (a Demandware cartridge). The PWA never makes the call; credentials live in SFCC Business Manager.
* **via MuleSoft** — SFCC-side, server-to-server through the MuleSoft middleware. The PWA never sees the downstream system.
* **Out-of-band** — runs outside the storefront runtime entirely (scheduled feed, build-time pipeline, or system-to-system integration that bypasses the PWA and often SFCC too).

A single integration can span multiple classes — e.g. Adyen is `SFCC-cartridge` for `/payments` calls and `Browser-direct` for the Drop-In SDK; Global-e is `Browser-direct` (checkout handoff — iframe embed) and `SFCC-cartridge` (pricing feed); GiveX is `via MuleSoft` / server-side NewStore-adapter for issue/validate/redeem/refund and `MRT-mediated` for balance checks. Compound rows list every class that applies.

> Reading the table: **Call origin** = where the network request is issued from. **Hosting layer** = which boundary class above. **Security** = how credentials are exposed.

8. SSR, SEO, and GEO Foundation
-------------------------------

### 8.1 SSR (DMU-030)

All product, category, and content pages will use SSR for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS. The PWA Kit SSR pipeline is preserved end-to-end. Any component that cannot render on the server is wrapped in a boundary that still outputs the required SEO markup server-side. Global state stores are initialised per request to prevent state leaking across SSR responses.

#### 8.1.1 SSR vs CSR by page type

PWA Kit always runs the SSR pipeline — every page is server-rendered to some degree. The practical distinction is what content is rendered on the server vs fetched client-side after hydration.

| Page type | Pattern | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PDP, PLP, content pages, homepages, boutique pages | **Full SSR** — markup and data rendered on the server | Indexable, SEO- and LCP-critical |
| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | **SSR shell + CSR data** — server renders the layout, header, footer, and skeleton; `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hydrates personalised data (basket lines, customer profile, orders) client-side after hydration | Personalised, per-session, behind authentication. No SEO value (blocked in `robots.txt` — §8.3). Server-rendering personalised data would defeat edge caching and risk state leaking across requests |
| Search results, filtered PLP states | **SSR shell + CSR data** | Blocked in `robots.txt`; filter / sort state is client-driven |

The "SSR shell + CSR data" pattern still gives the user instant first paint of the page chrome — only the personalised payload waits on hydration. No page is purely client-rendered.

### 8.2 Canonicals & hreflang

Canonical tags on every indexable page; filtered PLPs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP. hreflang on canonical PDPs only, delivered via XML sitemap, consolidated to ~12 regional/language-level tags. Detailed canonical/hreflang rules are specified in the functional requirements.

### 8.3 Sitemaps & robots

Per-storefront / per-locale XML sitemaps refreshed daily, excluding disabled and deleted pages (DMU-026). `robots.txt` permits indexable pages (including the bag page) and blocks checkout, account, search results, and filtered URL parameters. URLs blocked in `robots.txt` never appear in a sitemap.

### 8.4 Structured data

Custom JSON-LD per the Sparro templates, rendered server-side so crawlers see it on the first response:

* **PDP:** Product + Merchant Listing Schema (`ProductGroup` + variant `Product`s), with real-time inventory driving availability.
* **PLP:** CollectionPage + BreadcrumbList + ItemList Schema (ItemList reflects the initial SSR'd product batch).
* **Boutique pages:** LocalBusiness / ClothingStore Schema per location.
* **Homepages:** Organisation + WebSite Schema per regional storefront, with per-prefix `WebSite` nodes (including the Global-e international paths `/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/`).

### 8.5 URL strategy

* Product URL: `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` — the `.html` suffix is preserved to maintain existing indexed URLs.
* Category URL: `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no suffix), with 301 redirects from legacy paths.
* 301 redirects for every URL that changes as a result of migration (products, categories, content). Implemented at the CDN/edge layer to keep application-layer impact minimal.

### 8.6 Generative Engine Optimisation (DMU-042)

No GEO-specific features in launch scope. The technical foundations enabling post-launch GEO — SSR, structured data, canonicals, XML sitemaps — are in place at go-live so no architecture decision blocks future activation.

9. Performance Strategy
-----------------------

LCP at p75 mobile is the binding constraint and the de-facto cap on third-party script weight.

| Metric | Target |
| --- | --- |
| LCP (mobile p75) | ≤ 2 s |
| Lighthouse Performance | ≥ 0.80 |
| Lighthouse Accessibility | ≥ 0.90 |
| Lighthouse Best Practices | ≥ 0.90 |

### 9.1 Third-party defer rule

Every third-party script that loads via Didomi callback is deferred, asynchronously loaded, or injected after page load so it does not block LCP.

* **Measmerize** (PDP only) defers behind LCP — the script is injected after the product hero image has loaded.
* **reCAPTCHA** loads only on registration / login form interaction, so it is never on the critical path of any other page. Consent treatment: §11.1.
* **Optimizely Web (AAB-004) — the one exception:** it loads in the page head before the page renders, to prevent A/B test flicker. US storefront only. Zimmermann provides the snippet; keep it minimal.
* **Crazy Egg (AAB-005):** loads asynchronously, strictly post-Didomi-consent — it does not block first paint.

### 9.2 Other levers

* **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
* **Video:** sourced by platform, not self-hosted, so codec / adaptive-streaming selection belongs to the upstream player rather than to this layer:

  + **Product videos → Vimeo**, referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS (PRD-067). Load behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS never lands on the LCP critical path.
  + **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
  + Across both: `preload="metadata"` by default; autoplay reserved for muted, short-loop hero clips only.
* Dynamic imports for heavy non-initial components.
* Parallel data fetches; no client-side waterfalls. Fetch only required fields.

### 9.3 Where performance is measured

The CI Lighthouse gate (§14.3) catches regressions but runs against the Dev-tier MRT deployment — slower than production hardware, further from the edge, and not representative of the LCP a real shopper experiences. 12. Graceful Degradation
------------------------

Each external system fails independently — one outage does not break a page.

| System | Failure mode |
| --- | --- |
| Contentful | Render page without editorial content; never block commerce data on CMS |
| Global-e | Surface explicit error; do not silently fall back to SFCC for international checkout |
| Didomi | Fail closed — no consent, no third-party scripts |
| Omneo (writes) / Emarsys | Queue and retry silently; never block the user flow |
| Omneo (reads) | **Load-bearing for My Account profile pages** — per DMU-004 only email + Omneo ID are migrated; all other customer profile data is sourced live from Omneo at login. Surface an explicit retry/error UI on profile pages if the round-trip fails; do not render stale or partial profile data. |
| Google Maps | Degrade to manual address entry; never hard-block checkout |
| AP21 (Retail Rewards) | On AP21 unavailability at the point of Rewards application, inform the customer and allow an alternative payment method |
| Narvar (EDD) | Suppress widget; do not show an error or block checkout |

### 12.1 Blast-Radius Containment

The failure modes above describe what the PWA does when a single integration is unavailable. This section covers how to limit the *spread* of an attack or outage — ensuring a degraded integration cannot consume shared resources and take down unrelated features.

#### Edge (outside the PWA — Infrastructure / SI Partner)

* **Web Application Firewalls + rate limiting** is the primary lever for volumetric attacks and credential-stuffing.
* **SFCC Business Manager** provides API-level rate limiting for SFCC endpoints, independent of the storefront edge.

#### SSR layer (inside the PWA)

The SSR layer makes server-side fetch calls for token exchange, JWKS validation, and payment method metadata. Each upstream origin is assigned its own connection pool with an independent concurrency cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration — such as a checkout API under load — from exhausting connections for unrelated origins such as Contentful or the SLAS JWKS endpoint.

| Pool | Upstream | Isolated because |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SFCC SCAPI | SLAS JWKS endpoint | Token-validation calls are infrequent (JWK set is cached); they must not be starved by commerce traffic |
| SFCC Payments | Payment method metadata | Called on every checkout page SSR; a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections |
| MuleSoft | MuleSoft base URL | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP); GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials and must not be queued behind other traffic |
| Google Places | Google Maps Places API | Non-critical path; a Places API slowdown must not hold connections open for other integrations |
| Booxi | Booxi API | My Account only; low concurrency |

Security - **Secrets**: never committed — real values in gitignored `.env.`/`.env.shared`, injected as MRT env vars on deploy. `.env.sample` is template-only (names, no values). `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` blocks a commit if a secret-class key (`*_TOKEN`, `*_API_KEY`, `*_DSN`, etc.) has a non-empty value or matches a known credential pattern (JWT, AWS `AKIA…`, GitHub `ghp_`, Slack `xox…`). - **Payment credentials**: never logged/persisted client-side, submitted only in POST bodies, masked after submit (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`) — enforced by the `payment-credential-logged` semgrep rule. - **XSS**: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must wrap a sanitizer call — enforced by the `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` semgrep rule. - **CodeRabbit** (`coderabbit.yaml`) additionally wires in `gitleaks` (secret scanning), `osvScanner` (dependency CVEs), `eslint`, `reactDoctor`, and ast-grep — all as advisory PR-review signal, not a merge gate. - **Env-var security boundary table** ([TSD §4.1](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585)): every integration credential is classified browser-direct (public) vs MRT-mediated (server-only) vs CI-only — e.g. Contentful Preview/Management tokens, MuleSoft/Booxi/GiveX credentials, and reCAPTCHA secret key never reach the browser bundle. - **Blast-radius containment** (same TSD §12.1): per-upstream SSR connection pools so a flooded integration (e.g. checkout) can't starve unrelated ones (Contentful, SLAS JWKS). - **Consent fails closed**: unknown consent state → no third-party script loads at all (Didomi). ## 3. Development process - Four-step workflow enforced by AGENTS.md: clarify → plan → copy-first (base template files copied to `overrides/` with a marker `console.log` before functional changes) → implement, with an optional local CodeRabbit pass before commit. - TypeScript-only inside `overrides/`, strict mode; no `any` without a comment; DRY/KISS/SOLID; no magic numbers; Australian spelling for Zimmermann code. - **No mocking in production paths** — all data from live Commerce Cloud API. - **Minimal-changes rule**: no upward refactors, no renaming shared hooks/components, no silent scope creep. - Git hooks: `commit-msg` enforces Conventional Commits; `pre-commit` also regenerates derived AI-config files and Contentful `definitions.ts`, and blocks hand-edits to derived config files bypassing their source. ## 4. Delivery / CI-CD gates - **`qa.yml`** (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): unit tests always run; Storybook interaction + a11y and Playwright are path-scoped to the diff (change-scoped E2E); BrowserStack cross-browser only runs when a Jira key is detected in the PR (develop) or unscoped on `release/**`. - **`digital-sit.yml` / Digital SIT Gate** (required check on `release/**`): Playwright P0 (100% pass, 0 retries — flaky tests must be fixed not retried), Lighthouse CI (Perf ≥80, A11y ≥90, Best Practices ≥90, no >5pt regression), MuleSoft contract tests (currently a **placeholder**, exits 0 — open dependency pending MuleSoft OpenAPI spec), bundle size (`main.js`<180kB, `vendor.js`<250kB, `main.css`<50kB via bundlewatch). - **Deploy workflows**: `deploy-dev` auto on push to `develop` (gated on contract-tests+bundle-size); `deploy-sit` auto after SIT Gate passes; `deploy-uat`/`deploy-stg`/`deploy-prod` are all manual `workflow_dispatch` only, each behind its own GitHub `environment:` (reviewer protection configured at repo-settings level). - **STAGE promotion** is a manual, non-automated checklist: SIT Gate green + NewStore SIT complete + Integration Lead/squad-lead sign-off. - Weekly automation: `upstream-release-watch.yml` flags new `@salesforce/retail-react-app` releases; `weekly-agents.yml` flags missing tests/stories, Contentful drift, and changelog gaps. ## 5. Testing / QA - 3 layers, no duplicated coverage: Vitest (logic), Storybook `play` (interaction), Playwright (E2E) — see `.claude/rules/testing.md`. - **Gherkin-first workflow**: `.feature` file → Lead QA sign-off in plain English → Playwright spec generated only after approval. - **Multi-region fixtures** from day one (7 storefronts × 11 locales) — no hardcoded region. - **AI-Assisted QA six-stage pipeline** ([overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/277544962)) with three mandatory human gates: BA approves AC (Gate 1), Tester approves Zephyr cases (Gate 2), Developer reviews any agent-raised fix PR (Gate 3) — the triage agent never touches Tier 1 files, always raises a Jira defect instead. ## 6. Accessibility - Target WCAG 2.2 AA (2.1 AA floor). Mechanically enforced via `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`: missing ``, missing `IconButton aria-label`, clickable non-interactive elements missing `role`. Plus `vitest-axe`, `axe-playwright`, Storybook a11y addon, and the Lighthouse A11y ≥90 CI threshold. ## 7. Performance - LCP ≤2s p75 mobile is the binding constraint. All Didomi-gated third-party scripts must defer/async/post-hydration load (documented exception: Optimizely Web loads pre-render to avoid flicker, US-only). Bundle-size ceilings enforced in CI (above). ## 8. Consent, privacy & graceful degradation - Didomi gates every third-party script, fails closed on unknown consent. Marketing opt-in unchecked by default except US (pre-checked); syncs FE→SFCC→Omneo→Emarsys, retries silently, never blocks checkout. GDPR (DSAR/erasure) handled by the SFCC cartridge. Each external integration has a documented failure mode (§12 of the TSD) — e.g. Global-e failure surfaces an explicit error rather than silently falling back to SFCC checkout; Omneo reads are load-bearing for My Account and must show explicit retry UI rather than partial data. ## 9. Release & dependency policy - Supervised editing on `release/*`/`hotfix/*` per `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`; GitFlow back-merges mandatory to keep `develop` aligned. - Upstream `@salesforce/retail-react-app` bumps are opportunistic (security/CVE or a wanted fix), never scheduled, per `.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`. ## Known gaps / exceptions worth knowing about - The SIT gate's MuleSoft contract-test check is a no-op placeholder. - reCAPTCHA provides no bot protection in EU/UK for consent-declining visitors (accepted tradeoff). - GitHub Environment Variables (used for centralized shared/tier config) are plaintext-readable by collaborators — a deliberate, documented exception to the secrets policy, gated to `tier-1-approvers` only. - Per an earlier Confluence read, the "Development Standards" and "Component Override Strategy" pages still describe a `custom/` sub-folder for new components and a direct-import icon pattern that both contradict current AGENTS.md/repo convention — worth flagging to whoever owns those pages.
